billingAccount.description:
BillingAccount is the billing account identifier. Required for both agreement types.

Example (super-catchy, isn't it): aaa111b-abcd-ef01-2345-bcdabc123fed:1234aaab-0100-1234-abcd-abcd0123abcd_2019-05-31

billingProfile.description:
BillingProfile defined for an MCA agreement type which billing profile contains the invoice section you wish subscriptions to be created in. Required for MCA.

Example: AW4F-APQW-0AH-ABC

contributorObjectID.description:
ContributorObjectID specifies an optional object ID of an Azure AD group, user or service principal to grant Contributor privilege on all created subscriptions.

Example: 8bf96a8f-dcef-abc1-a389-883d6116a5da

enrollmentAccount.description:
EnrollmentAccount defines for an Enterprise Agreement agreement type which enrollment account to create subscriptions within. Required for EA.

Example: 7654321

invoiceSection.description:
InvoiceSection defines for an MCA agreement type which invoice section to create subscriptions within inside the selected BillingProfile. Required for MCA.

Example: PQRS-ALDS-012-DEF

managementGroupID.description:
ManagementGroupID specifies an optional ID of an Azure Management Group in which subscriptions created by Wayfinder should be placed.

Example: wf-subscription-mgt-group

ownerObjectID.description:
OwnerObjectID specifies the Object ID of an Azure AD group, user or service principal to grant Owner privilege on all created subscriptions. This is required to ensure that generated subscriptions are owned by an object controlled by your company.

Example: 8bf96a8f-abcd-ef12-a389-883d6116a5da

This includes time before being scheduled as well as time spent downloading images over the network, which could take a while. Running: The pod has been bound to a node, and all of the containers have been created. At least one container is still running, or is in the process of starting or restarting. Succeeded: All containers in the pod have terminated in success, and will not be restarted. Failed: All containers in the pod have terminated, and at least one container has terminated in failure. The container either exited with non-zero status or was terminated by the system. Unknown: For some reason the state of the pod could not be obtained, typically due to an error in communicating with the host of the pod.

More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/pod-lifecycle#pod-phase

version.description: Version is the kubernetes version of the cluster

hardQuota.description:
QuotaHard are applied as ResourceQuota objects to all namespaces for a tenant of that type There are the maximun resource usage in total for a namespace e.g.: hardQuota:

limitRanges.description: LimitRanges (in the context of constraints) are applied as LimitRanges (using Max) These are the largest values that can be used by a single resource in a namespace They will prevent workloads from using up all resources on a single node

autoscaling.description: Autoscaling indicates the node pool should autoscale

channel.description: Channel describes the channel a NodePool follows If specified on a cluster, must be identical to the channel on the cluster

cloudResourceName.description: CloudResourceName is the name of the cloud resource - should not be set by the client - set by the NodePool mutate if empty - set by the NodePoolUpdate controller depending on the update type

defaultUpdateOptions.description: DefaultUpdateOptions defines how this nodepool can be upgraded - Used by the cluster controller to generate NodePoolUpdates based on spec changes - Ignored when a NodePoolUpdate is created directly

description.description: Description provides an optional description to the node pool

diskSize.description: DiskSize is the amount of disk space to assign to the nodes in MBs

expires.description: Expires provides a time for automatic expiration of the cluster

image.description: Image is the image we should use on the instances of this pool

labels.description: Labels is a collection of label placed on to the nodepool

logicalName.description: LogicalName is the internally unique name of the NodePool (not in cloud) - Should always be consistent with a single name entry in a Cluster or NodePoolUpdate - Has to be unique across all nodepools on the Cluster spec - Will NOT always match the name of the NodePool in cloud - Should be treated as an immutable field

machine.description: Machine is the instance type of the nodes in the poll

maxPodsPerNode.description: MaxPodsPerNode controls how many pods can be scheduled onto each node in this pool

providerDetails.description: ProviderDetails provides any cloud specific options for this nodepool

size.description: Size is initial size if autoscaling defined - or the effective size if no autoscaling is enabled

spot.description: Spot if defines enables nodepool to use spot instances

taints.description: Taints defines a collection scheduling taints placed on the nodepool

version.description: Version is the specified version of kubernetes on the node pool This cannot be set by a client if a channel is also specified Will be set by the NodePoolUpdate controller on actual nodepools if a channel is specified

zones.description: Zones defines a list of cloud specific availability zones where the nodes are permitted to run

name.description: Name is the name of the node pool

nodeCount.description: NodeCount is the number of nodes in the node pool

nodeCountReady.description: NodeCountReady is the number of nodes in the node pool which are ready

providerStatus.description: ProvisioningState is provisioning state of the nodePool

migrated.description: Migrated is true if the node has been successfully migrated to the new node pool

DeletionTimestamp is RFC 3339 date and time at which this resource will be deleted. The resource is expected to be deleted (no longer visible from resource lists, and not reachable by name) after the time in this field, once the finalizers list is empty. cidrBlocks.description:
CIDRBlocks is a list of CIDR blocks that are associated with the network. provider.description: Provider refers to the cloud provider.

v1.SecretReference.description: SecretReference represents a Secret Reference. It has enough information to retrieve secret in any namespace

name.description: name is unique within a namespace to reference a secret resource.

namespace.description: namespace defines the space within which the secret name must be unique.

v1.Subject.description: Subject contains a reference to the object or user identities a role binding applies to.  This can either hold a direct API object reference, or a value for non-objects such as user and group names.

apiGroup.description: APIGroup holds the API group of the referenced subject. Defaults to "" for ServiceAccount subjects. Defaults to "rbac.authorization.k8s.io" for User and Group subjects.

kind.description: Kind of object being referenced. Values defined by this API group are "User", "Group", and "ServiceAccount". If the Authorizer does not recognized the kind value, the Authorizer should report an error.

name.description: Name of the object being referenced.

namespace.description: Namespace of the referenced object.  If the object kind is non-namespace, such as "User" or "Group", and this value is not empty the Authorizer should report an error.
